nodes.label: Data Honesty Principle
nodes.rationale: Every number in the UI must come from the database. SAMPLE fixtures are deliberately and visibly fake (names prefixed SAMPLE, source_url = SAMPLE, yellow banner) so the app can run before real data exists without the demo ever being mistaken for verified findings. Unverified real rows are marked <<FILL>> and skipped at load with a warning rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Evidence Index (uncalibrated)
nodes.rationale: Scoring is a weighted points sum divided by 100, deliberately labelled 'Evidence index (uncalibrated)' and never called a probability, because the weights are hand-chosen and not fit to outcomes. Tiers: verified >= 0.7, likely >= 0.4, else low.

nodes.label: As-of Query Pattern
nodes.rationale: A score dated D uses only evidence dated on or before D (whole day, UTC), implemented as ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1 over the (project_id, ts DESC) index. This makes the whole dashboard rewindable without recomputation and prevents future evidence leaking into past scores.

nodes.label: Shell LLC to Parent Resolution
nodes.rationale: Data-center projects are filed under shell LLCs, so each LLC is resolved to a parent company with a recorded resolved_by method (COMPTROLLER, TDLR_TENANT, MANUAL) plus a source_url, keeping the provenance of every attribution auditable.

nodes.label: Idempotent Upsert Loading
nodes.rationale: Unique indexes on entities.llc_name and projects.name let loads upsert by name, and evidence rows carry a payload._origin marker so a reload replaces only rows that the same script inserted. This makes run_all.py safely re-runnable after any CSV edit.

nodes.label: gridsight_ro read-only role
nodes.rationale: The web app connects as gridsight_ro with a 3 s statement timeout so dashboard and LLM-driven queries cannot write or hang the database.

nodes.label: Gemini Function-Calling Tool Set
nodes.rationale: Gemini is given exactly four tools (filter_projects, get_project_timeline, get_summary, compare_parents) that call the same query functions as the REST API, and never free-form SQL, with at most 4 tool rounds. This bounds the model's database access to vetted, parameterized queries.

nodes.label: <<FILL>> placeholder convention
nodes.rationale: Any cell containing <<FILL>> counts as missing; rows missing a required field are skipped and listed in the output rather than loaded with guessed values, so the team can see exactly what still needs verification.

nodes.label: TimescaleDB Testing Caveat
nodes.rationale: The stack was tested end to end on local PostgreSQL 17 with stand-ins for create_hypertable, time_bucket, last() and refresh_continuous_aggregate, and never against a real Tiger Cloud instance; Ask GridSight was only tested at tool-dispatch level because no Gemini key was available.

nodes.label: Next.js agent rules block
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. The block is regenerated by next dev, so it should be committed rather than stripped from diffs.
